questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must have all three documents in your vehicle while driving.

questions.question: You should never park a vehicle:

options.text: Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Within 30 feet of any flashing signal on the side of a roadway.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, within 20 feet of a crosswalk, or within 30 feet of a signal light, stop sign, or flashing beacon on the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a sharp turn coming up. You should slow down.

questions.question: When daylight is fading, use your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades so others can see you. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers present.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Stay alert, slow down, follow signs and flaggers, and be ready to react to hazards.
Speed up so you don't slow down traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert, slow down, follow signs and flaggers, and be ready to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and watch the traffic around you. Follow all signs and directions from flaggers. Be ready to respond quickly to any changes.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use proper headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are completely out of your way.
Honk your horn and drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are completely out of your way.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person using a white cane or guide dog, stop your vehicle. Wait until they have crossed and are well away from you. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then drive across once the gates rise.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then drive across once the gates rise.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when you see warning signs or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep makes you a worse driver. Like drugs and alcohol, tiredness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and affects your judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The safe speed limit for a residential area.
The safe speed limit for an expressway exit.
The safe speed limit for an expressway entrance.
The safe speed limit for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed limit for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a three-point turn?

options.text: Signal and check your mirrors, then turn.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your left shoulder, and turn only when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your left shoulder, and turn only when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: To make a three-point turn: Stop near the right edge of the road. Look over your left shoulder to check for traffic. Signal a left turn. Then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Always signal when you move left or right. Use your signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only have a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol. It is dangerous to yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride.
questions.explanation: Bikes are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to avoid crashes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Turn your head and check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: If you take an over-the-counter drug, you should:

options.text: Read the label to see if it affects driving.
Drive anyway, even if there are warnings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label to see if it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where there are pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving once you think the children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases. At speeds over 80 mph, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right, then to the left.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance, increases crash risk, and slows your decisions. When tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash, injuring or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage becomes more common. To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus turns on its flashing red lights and stop arm when loading or unloading students. Do not proceed until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where should children age 12 and under sit?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags protect adults in crashes but can seriously injure children. Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no visible train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a stop sign, or a flagger signaling you to stop. If a train is visible or close enough to be unsafe, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For the best protection, always wear your lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane highway and approach a stopped school bus with red lights flashing. You:

options.text: May pass if the way is clear.
May pass if a pedestrian says it is safe.
Must wait until the bus driver turns off the lights and continues driving.
Must turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must wait until the bus driver turns off the lights and continues driving.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already in the roundabout.
